ANOTHER PLACE TO FLY. ANOTHER LEGACY PRESERVED. ✈️🌿

High Rock Airfield in western Maryland has a new chapter—and recreational pilots have another special destination to discover.

The Recreational Aviation Foundation has become steward of the airfield following a gift from Bob Armstrong’s estate. The 1,700-foot turf strip sits along the North Branch of the Potomac River, about 85 nautical miles northwest of Washington, D.C.

Bob and his father, Harold, shared a passion for restoring vintage aircraft. Preserving the airfield for future aviators carries that family legacy forward.

RAF says High Rock is now registered with the FAA as 68MD. Visitors can enjoy riverside camping and seasonal trout fishing, with aviation fellowship at the heart of the experience.

Planning a visit? Start with RAF’s Airfield Guide and required safety briefing before making flight plans. A short turf strip calls for careful aircraft, performance and conditions planning.

Here’s to the families and volunteers keeping places like this on the map—and giving the next generation somewhere wonderful to fly. 💛

Sources: Recreational Aviation Foundation, October 30, 2026; General Aviation News, November 4, 2026.
